title: The mod-two square algebra, admissible sequences, and excess
statement:
Let $T=\mathbb F_2\langle s_1,s_2,\ldots\rangle$ be the vector space with basis the finite words in the symbols $s_j$ for $j>0$, including the empty word, and with multiplication the bilinear extension of concatenation. Concatenation is associative and the empty word is its unit, so this explicitly constructs the free associative graded algebra, with $|s_j|=j$ and $s_0=1$. Define $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}$ as its quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by

\[
s_a s_b+\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor a/2\rfloor}
\binom{b-j-1}{a-2j}s_{a+b-j}s_j,
\qquad 0<a<2b.
\]

A normalized sequence $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ has positive entries; the empty sequence denotes the unit. It is admissible if $i_j\ge 2i_{j+1}$. Write $|I|=\sum_j i_j$, put $i_{k+1}=0$, and define

\[
d_j(I)=i_j-2i_{j+1},\qquad
 e(I)=\sum_{j=1}^k d_j(I)=i_1-i_2-\cdots-i_k.
\]

For the empty sequence set $|I|=e(I)=0$. The square algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ is the image of the free algebra under $s_j\mapsto Sq^j$ in natural mod-two cohomology operations, allowing every nonnegative input degree. The published Adem theorem makes the induced map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ well defined. Item 4 proves it is an isomorphism.
strategy: Construct the free associative word algebra by concatenation, then take its quotient by the homogeneous two-sided Adem ideal. Verify representative independence, associativity, the unit and quotient grading directly. Define degree, admissibility and excess by finite sums, including the empty word; the nonnegative admissibility differences telescope to excess. The published Adem relations give the quotient-to-square-operation map. Naturality, linearity, composition and the published suspension identity give its stable image algebra. Spanning, independence and the presentation are proved by Items 2–4; no classification of all stable operations is assumed.

title: Adem reduction spans by admissible square composites
statement: In degree $N\ge0$, every element of $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}$ is a finite linear combination of the admissible words $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$ with $|I|=N$. Consequently the same is true in $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$.
strategy: In degree N pad normalized positive sequences with terminal zeros to length N and order the finite set lexicographically. Each Adem replacement of a nonadmissible adjacent pair (a,b) replaces it by (a+b-j,j) with j<b, so its first changed entry strictly increases. Removing a terminal identity after that entry preserves the increase. Descending induction on this finite order terminates in admissible words, preserving total degree. The unit handles degree zero. Pass through the quotient-to-operation map to obtain the operation spanning assertion without assuming independence.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 4.L, printed p. 499: lexicographic Adem reduction.

title: Admissible square actions have distinct leading monomials
statement:
Assume AC. Let $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ be admissible, let $r\ge e(I)$, and choose $L\ge |I|+1$. On

\[
 X=(\mathbb{RP}^{L})^r,
 \qquad H^*(X;\mathbb F_2)=
 \mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^{L+1},\ldots,x_r^{L+1}),
\]

put $P=x_1\cdots x_r$. Order monomials lexicographically by their exponent vectors, largest first. The largest monomial of $Sq^I(P)$ has coefficient one and has exponents

\[
(\underbrace{2^k,\ldots,2^k}_{d_k},
 \underbrace{2^{k-1},\ldots,2^{k-1}}_{d_{k-1}},
 \ldots,
 \underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{d_1},
 \underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-e(I)}).
\]

For fixed total degree $|I|$, different admissible sequences have different largest monomials. The empty sequence gives $P$.
strategy: Compute finite projective-space cohomology and its product ring using the published cellular and finite-free Künneth interfaces. Cartan and the top-square identity give Sq^a(x^m)=binom(m,a)x^(m+a); for m a power of two the only possible actions are no change or doubling. Regard each composite as a finite schedule of doublings. For a sequence of length k, at most i_k variables can reach exponent 2^k; reaching that maximum forces their complete doubling chains. Subtract their forced costs from the earlier budgets and induct on the residual admissible sequence. This proves both maximality and coefficient one, with multiplicities d_k,…,d_1. The exponent bound 1+|I| prevents truncation; backward recursion recovers I from these multiplicities. Distinct leading terms, rather than disjoint supports, prove the asserted distinction.

title: Admissible composites present the mod-two square algebra
statement: Assume AC. The natural map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Adem}}\to\mathcal A_{\mathrm{Sq}}$ is an isomorphism. In each degree $N$, its admissible composites $Sq^I$ with $|I|=N$ form an $\mathbb F_2$-basis. Thus the Adem relations impose all algebraic relations among composites of the published Steenrod squares.
strategy: Adem reduction spans the abstract quotient by admissible words. For a putative nonzero homogeneous relation of degree N among their natural operations, evaluate every term on the same product class on (RP^(N+1))^(N+1). The leading-monomial lemma applies to every sequence. Its largest occurring leading monomial cannot cancel against terms with smaller leading monomials, so the relation is nonzero. The identity is nonzero in degree zero. Since the quotient relations are homogeneous, degreewise independence makes the already surjective quotient-to-operation map injective.

title: The universal mod-two class detects admissible composites in the strict range
statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$ let $K_q=K(\mathbb F_2,q)$ be a based CW model with its normalized fundamental class $\iota_q$. For $0\le i<q$, the map

\[
 \eta_{q,i}:\mathcal A^i\longrightarrow
 \widetilde H^{q+i}(K_q;\mathbb F_2),\qquad
 a\longmapsto a(\iota_q)
\]

is injective. If $f:X\to K_q$ classifies $z\in\widetilde H^q(X;\mathbb F_2)$, then $f^*\eta_{q,i}(a)=a(z)$.
strategy: Representability supplies the normalized universal class and its based classifying maps; square naturality gives the evaluation identity. Expand a nonzero degree-i operation in the admissible basis and evaluate it on the degree-q product of degree-one generators on (RP^(i+1))^q. Since every excess is at most i<q, the common leading-term test is nonzero. A classifying map pulls the universal evaluation back to this test, so vanishing universally is impossible. This includes the identity and the q=1 strict range.

references.title: Tom Weston, An Introduction to Cobordism Theory
references.locator: Section 8, printed p. 15: universal evaluation on Eilenberg–Mac Lane classes.

title: Local path-fibration and cohomology inputs for mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane induction
statement: Assume AC. For $q\ge2$, $K_q$ is simply connected, $\widetilde H^j(K_q;\mathbb F_2)=0$ for $j<q$, and $H^q(K_q;\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb F_2\iota_q$. The actual contractible mapping-path fibration has strict loop fiber $F=\Omega K_q$. There is a marked weak equivalence $h:K_{q-1}\to F$ inducing an isomorphism of mod-two cohomology rings $h^*:H^*(F;\mathbb F_2)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*(K_{q-1};\mathbb F_2)$. Its natural multiplicative cohomological Serre spectral sequence has constant fiber system. No claim that $F$ has CW homotopy type or that $h$ is a homotopy equivalence is needed. In particular its abutment vanishes in positive degrees.
strategy: Use ordinary Hurewicz and cohomology UCT on the CW base to obtain its lower vanishing and normalized first class. Apply direct mapping-path factorization to the marked basepoint inclusion; the actual total contracts, and the fibration LES computes the connected strict loop fiber's marking and homotopy groups. Extend its basepoint by a weak CW approximation, identify that CW model with the marked K(F_2,q-1) by uniqueness, and adjust the uniqueness map to be based via the CW-point cofibration and moving-basepoint formula. Their composite is a marked weak equivalence. The published weak-equivalence homology lemma, natural coefficient UCT and field duality make its cohomology map an isomorphism; cup naturality makes it a ring isomorphism. Apply the multiplicative Serre theorem to the actual fibration with trivial monodromy. No strict-fiber CW-type theorem is imported.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 4.2, printed pp. 376–377: the path-space fibration; Section 4.1, Proposition 4.13: CW approximation. The required strict-fiber cohomology comparison is proved locally via the published weak-equivalence homology and coefficient interfaces.

title: Infinite real projective space is a marked mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane space
statement: Assume AC. Infinite real projective space, with the marking of its fundamental group given by the nontrivial antipodal deck transformation, is a CW $K(\mathbb F_2,1)$. Its degree-one ring generator is its normalized mod-two fundamental class, so its cohomology is $\mathbb F_2[\iota_1]$.
strategy: Identify the stable sphere and rank-one Grassmannian models. Coordinate-positive unit representatives give local sections of the antipodal double cover; their finite-stage formulas are continuous in the weak topologies. The covering homotopy-lifting theorem makes it a fibration, and stable Stiefel contractibility gives no higher base homotopy. Endpoint deck transformations identify the fundamental group with Z/2, with injectivity from a contraction of a closed lifted loop and surjectivity from a path joining antipodes. Schubert cells give the CW structure. The published polynomial projective-space cohomology ring has a unique nonzero degree-one class, which is therefore the normalized fundamental class. Marked uniqueness transfers it to the chosen CW model.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory
references.locator: Section 1.2, printed pp. 28–31: stable sphere, Grassmannian and universal bundle models.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

title: Steenrod squares commute with relative cohomology connectors
statement: For every pair $(E,F)$, the mod-two cohomology connector satisfies $\delta Sq^a(x)=Sq^a\delta(x)$ for every $x\in H^m(F;\mathbb F_2)$ and every nonnegative $a$. Relative squares use the published relative cup-$i$ construction.
strategy: Extend a fiber cocycle u by zero to a cochain b on the ambient space and put c=db, a relative representative of the connector. For 0≤a≤m set j=m-a. The cochain b cup_(j+1) db + b cup_j b restricts to a representative of Sq^a[u], and the published cup-i coboundary identity makes its coboundary c cup_(j+1) c, representing Sq^a[c]. At a=m+1 use the relative primitive b cup_0 db; larger operations vanish by instability. The relative carrier property and characteristic two justify all cancellations and relative representatives, including degree-zero inputs.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Lemma 1.35, printed p. 55: compatibility of squares with cohomological transgression; connector compatibility is proved cochain-wise in the local draft.

title: Relative lifts produce cohomological transgressions
statement:
Assume AC. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Serre fibration over a simply connected CW base with basepoint vertex and fiber $F$. If $x\in H^m(F;\mathbb F_2)$, $m>0$, and $y\in H^{m+1}(B,*;\mathbb F_2)$ satisfy

\[
 \delta x=p^*y\quad\text{in }H^{m+1}(E,F;\mathbb F_2),
\]

then $x$ survives to $E_{m+1}^{0,m}$ and its differential $d_{m+1}$ is the bottom-axis coset represented by $y$. Moreover $Sq^a x$ has the same property with representative $Sq^a y$ at page $m+a+1$, whenever its degree is positive.
strategy: Lift the base class y to cohomology relative to the m-skeleton, using cellular vanishing and the pair LES. Choose its cocycle v vanishing on that skeleton. Extend a representative of x to E and correct it by a cochain vanishing on F so that its coboundary is exactly p^*v. This lies in skeletal filtration m+1, giving survival to that page and the specified bottom-axis coset differential by the filtered page formulas and Serre base-edge construction. Connector compatibility and relative square naturality give the analogous relative lift for Sq^a x; repeat the same argument in its new total degree. No unproved operation on spectral-sequence pages is assumed.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Lemma 1.35, printed p. 55, and the relative construction underlying Proposition 1.13, printed pp. 21–22: relative lifts and transgression.

title: The fundamental path-fibration class has the normalized relative lift
statement:
Assume AC. For $n\ge1$, in the marked path fibration $F=\Omega K_{n+1}\to P K_{n+1}\xrightarrow p K_{n+1}$, with the fiber identified in marked homology and cohomology with $K_n$ by the weak equivalence of Item 6,

\[
 \delta\iota_n=p^*\iota_{n+1}
 \quad\text{in }H^{n+1}(P K_{n+1},F;\mathbb F_2).
\]
strategy: Represent the marked nonzero fiber homotopy class by a based sphere map. Its Hurewicz image is the nonzero integral homology generator: transfer ordinary CW Hurewicz through Item 6's weak equivalence for n>1, and use abelianization for n=1. Nullhomotope the sphere in the contractible path space to a disk lift A. Its finite disk fundamental chain defines a relative generator z, whose pair-LES boundary is the marked fiber generator. The collapsed projected disk represents the marked base homotopy class by the fibration connecting map. The good-pair quotient and natural cellular comparison identify p_*z with its base Hurewicz image. Verify the relative, base and fiber UCT Ext terms vanish, explicitly using connected H_0 for n=1. Both the connector and pulled-back fundamental class evaluate as one on z, so relative evaluation UCT identifies them. No relative Hurewicz theorem or fiber homotopy-equivalence premise is used.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.32, printed p. 55: the fundamental path-fibration transgression. Generator and UCT normalizations are proved locally using absolute Hurewicz and the pair long exact sequences.

title: Fiber and limit isomorphisms force a base-axis isomorphism
statement:
Let $\Phi:\bar E\to E$ be a morphism of first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequences of vector spaces, with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and

\[
 \bar E_2^{p,q}=\bar E_2^{p,0}\otimes\bar E_2^{0,q},\qquad
 E_2^{p,q}=E_2^{p,0}\otimes E_2^{0,q}.
\]

Assume $\Phi_2$ factors as the tensor product of its axis maps, the fiber-axis map is an isomorphism, and $\Phi_\infty$ is an isomorphism in every position. Then the base-axis map $\Phi_2^{p,0}$ is an isomorphism in every degree.
strategy: Induct on the base column k. The tensor factorization and fiber-axis isomorphism give E_2 isomorphisms through that column. Induction on r yields page-r isomorphisms in columns p≤k-r+1 and injections in columns p≤k, by comparing cycles and incoming boundaries. At the next bottom position (k+1,0), compare the incoming-differential exact sequences. For each incoming source, use finite downward induction from its stationary limit to prove surjectivity on its cycle subgroup; later outgoing differentials have negative fiber target. Starting from the limiting bottom isomorphism, descend in r using this cycle surjectivity and the other exact-sequence isomorphisms. This proves the next E_2 base-column isomorphism and closes the induction.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Theorem 1.36 and proof, printed pp. 56–58: fiber-axis and limiting isomorphisms imply the base-axis isomorphism.

title: A transgressive simple fiber system gives a polynomial base
statement:
Assume AC. Let $F\to E\to B$ be a Serre fibration with $E$ contractible and $B$ simply connected CW. The hypotheses concern the actual strict fiber cohomology ring; no CW-type or homotopy-equivalence assertion for the fiber is assumed. Suppose $H^*(F;\mathbb F_2)$ has a basis consisting of the finite products of **distinct** positive-degree classes $x_\lambda$, including the empty product, and only finitely many $x_\lambda$ occur in each degree. Suppose classes $y_\lambda\in H^{|x_\lambda|+1}(B,*;\mathbb F_2)$ satisfy $\delta x_\lambda=p^*y_\lambda$. Then

\[
 \mathbb F_2[Y_\lambda]\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*(B;\mathbb F_2),
 \qquad Y_\lambda\longmapsto y_\lambda.
\]

No assertion that $x_\lambda^2=0$ is required.
strategy: Build a model spectral sequence for each simple fiber generator with exterior x and polynomial Y, whose only differential is xY^a↦Y^(a+1) on page |x|+1. Tensor these factor sequences degreewise. Published vector-space bases and AC split complexes into homology plus contractible pairs; the tensor universal property, tensor/direct-sum and tensor-unit interfaces give the page-homology comparison, and H⊗id contracts each tensor pair. Positive degrees and local finiteness ensure only finitely many factors contribute per total degree. Evaluate squarefree fiber monomials and polynomial base monomials on the actual classes. Relative lifts and Leibniz give a morphism on every page; it is additive, not necessarily multiplicative in the fiber direction. The fiber axis and limiting scalar pages are isomorphic. Item 7d therefore identifies the base E_2 axis; there the map is the asserted polynomial ring homomorphism. Only computed strict-fiber cohomology is required.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Theorem 1.34 (Borel) and complete proof, printed pp. 54–56: transgressive simple systems and the polynomial-base spectral-sequence comparison.

title: Polynomial mod-two cohomology of Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$,

\[
 H^*(K_q;\mathbb F_2)
 \cong\mathbb F_2[Sq^I\iota_q\mid I\text{ admissible},\ e(I)<q],
\]

including the empty sequence, with the indicated classes as actual polynomial generators of degree $q+|I|$.
strategy: Prove the excess identities by instability and the top-square formula. An admissible sequence of excess q is uniquely obtained by repeatedly prepending the current class degree to a tail of excess <q; its value is the corresponding binary power. Start from the polynomial K(F_2,1) computation. Assuming the polynomial result for K_q, binary exponents give a simple system of distinct-power generators indexed bijectively by admissible sequences of excess ≤q, finite in every degree. Use Item 6's actual path fibration and weak-equivalence ring comparison to transfer this system to its strict fiber. Item 7c gives the fundamental relative lift; connector compatibility and naturality give all composite lifts, and Item 7b gives their exact transgressions, including the fiber class in degree 2q and all higher powers. Apply Item 7e to obtain the polynomial base generators with excess <q+1, proving generation and independence simultaneously.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1
references.locator: Theorem 1.32, Lemma 1.33 and induction proof, printed pp. 53–55; Theorem 1.34 and comparison Theorem 1.36, printed pp. 54–58.

title: Metastable cohomology of mod-two Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
statement:
Assume AC. For $q\ge1$ and $0\le i<q$, evaluation on the normalized mod-two fundamental class is an isomorphism

\[
 \eta_{q,i}:\mathcal A^i\xrightarrow{\cong}
 \widetilde H^{q+i}(K(\mathbb F_2,q);\mathbb F_2),\qquad
 a\longmapsto a(\iota_q).
\]

For a based classifying map $f$ of $z$, it satisfies $f^*\eta_{q,i}(a)=a(z)$. No integral identification and no degree-$2q$ endpoint claim is included.
strategy: The square algebra has the admissible basis by Item 4, independently of the EM computation. The polynomial presentation of Item 7 has generators of degrees at least q, so products of two positive generators cannot occur in degree q+i<2q. Its basis in that degree is exactly the single generators Sq^I iota_q with |I|=i; all admissible sequences of that degree have excess ≤i<q. Evaluation therefore takes the admissible operation basis bijectively to this cohomology basis. Item 5 also gives independent injectivity. Natural squares and the existing universal-operation corollary give the classifying-map formula. Include q=1,i=0 and make no degree-2q or integral identification.

references.locator: Corollary 1.38 and proof, printed pp. 58–59: evaluation in the metastable range; this record retains the strict inequality i<q.
